lines.text: Here's why Uber treats A I agents like insiders, in under sixty seconds.
Every company watches its people for insider threats, because staff sometimes act outside their role. Frontier models, the most capable A I, carry the same risk.
Say an agent is about to send customer data to a site Uber doesn't want.
First, every request passes through a gateway, a perimeter that controls how A I gets used.
Second, safeguards built with Anthropic check what the models produce, and Uber decides what happens when one fires.
Third, a system called A I Detection and Response watches in real time and catches the agent acting outside its bounds.
It steps in, close to the person typing, with a nudge like, you probably don't want to do that.
Then analysts hunt for behavior nobody expected and feed it back into the safeguards.
But new limits create new behavior, so the loop never ends.
